title: Trust accounting (Ontario By-Law 9)
summary: Books and controls for client money held in trust: pooled (mixed) and separate interest-bearing accounts, per-client ledgers, receipts and disbursements journals, transfers, withdrawals, bank feed matching, monthly three-way reconciliation and LSO annual report support. The agent posts, matches, checks and drafts. Money never moves, and no month is closed, without a named licensee's authorization. Every entry is append-only and fully audited.

screens.name: Trust overview
screens.purpose: Shows the trust position and every open exception on one page, so the responsible lawyer knows what needs action today.
screens.layout: Top: one balance card per trust account (bank balance, book balance, sum of client ledgers, a match light). Middle: an exceptions queue. Right: pending approvals (withdrawals, reconciliations) and the next reconciliation due date.

screens.reg: BL9: trust money goes in an account at an eligible institution, titled as trust. A mixed account's interest is paid to the Law Foundation of Ontario under the Law Society Act (verify). A separate interest-bearing account holds money for one client, with interest for that client (verify). An electronic transfer must be initiated by a licensee, or exceptionally by a bonded non-licensee with signing authority (BL9 s.12).

screens.agent: Builds proposed receipts from bank lines and payment-processor payouts, matches them to retainer requests and bills, checks the client's cumulative cash on the file against the limit, and warns when ID verification is missing before funds are accepted.
screens.gate: Gate G6: a human confirms each proposed receipt's client ledger and trust or general classification. A lawyer signs off on any cash over the limit, naming the exception.
edge: A payer sends a single amount that covers several matters: split into one line per client ledger
Money that belongs in general (payment of a delivered bill) arrives in trust: flag it and withdraw it promptly, per the withdrawal rules (verify)
Card-processor fees must not be taken from trust: card payments for retainers settle gross to trust, and fees are charged to general
Cash in foreign currency is converted to CAD for the limit check (verify)
Posting into a month that is already reconciled and locked is blocked; a dated correction is posted in the current month instead
screens.reg: BL9 s.18(1): trust receipts journal (date, method, payer, amount, purpose, client). Cash: a licensee may not receive cash aggregating $7,500 CAD or more on one client file (trust and operating receipts counted together; 749,999 cents allowed, 750,000 refused), subject to listed exceptions such as payment from a financial institution or public body, or fees where a refund over $7,500 is paid in cash (BL9 s.4 and s.6, verify). Client ID verification is required when funds are received, paid or transferred (By-Law 7.1, verify).

screens.agent: Fills in the request, then runs checks: the purpose is permitted; a bill was delivered for fees; the amount is within the cleared balance; no trust condition blocks release; the payee matches the direction; ID is verified; the bank details match a known payee, and a new or changed payee triggers a fraud warning. It then generates Form 9A and, after execution, reconciles the confirmation to the request.
screens.gate: G11: a licensee with signing authority authorizes the exact amount, payee, account and purpose. In dual mode, a second authorized person approves the transfer that the first person entered. The agent cannot authorize or execute.
edge: Funds are deposited but not cleared: the request is blocked (default hard block). A lawyer override with reason 'uncleared_override' under G11 exists only if the firm owner turns it on (owner decision, verify policy)
Payee bank details changed by email: hard stop with a callback requirement (fraud)
Withdrawal for fees where the bill is not yet delivered: blocked
The authorizing lawyer is also the client or payee: a second licensee is required
Bank confirmation does not arrive within one banking day: exception (verify timing)
A partial withdrawal leaves a small residue: the agent suggests a refund at closing
cheque spoiled in printer: void and reprint with the next number; both logged
screens.reg: BL9 s.9 (permitted withdrawals), s.10 (methods for fees and reimbursements), s.11 (no cash, verify) and s.12 (electronic transfers). Conditions in s.12: each user has a unique login; the system produces a confirmation right after the transfer showing the account numbers and the date and time; the initiator is a licensee or a bonded non-licensee with signing authority; a requisition (Form 9A) is signed before the transfer (verify); the confirmation is printed or kept and checked against the requisition within set timing (verify). Form 9A has a section for dual authorization. Forms were renumbered in a November 2025 amendment (verify).

screens.agent: Assembles the comparison, itemizes the reconciling items, explains each variance in plain language (for example, 'cheque 001288 issued 10-07, not yet cleared'), flags shortages that need immediate replenishment, and reminds the lawyer as the due date nears.
screens.gate: G12: the responsible licensee reviews and signs the monthly comparison and its explanations. A month cannot be signed while there is an unexplained difference or a negative client balance.
edge: Shortage found: an immediate replenishment task from the firm's own funds, and the reconciliation records it (verify reporting duty)
Prior month is not signed: the current month can be prepared but not signed
The bank statement arrives late: the due-date clock still runs
A reconciling item older than three months goes to the escalation list
preparer tries to force a $0 difference with an adjustment: blocked (deliberate)
reconciliation saved half-done: draft kept, due-date clock keeps running
reopen a month with later signed months: all later months shown and reopened together, their packages marked superseded
screens.reg: BL9 s.18(8): a monthly comparison of trust bank balances with client trust ledger totals, with the reasons for any difference, a detailed client listing and the bank reconciliations, kept as a record. It must be done within 25 days of month end (verify). Records are kept for 10 years before the most recent fiscal year end (verify). The signed package is kept for the full trust-record retention period.

screens.agent: Matches operating bank lines to bills paid and expenses, categorizes, and prepares the monthly operating reconciliation.
screens.gate: Bookkeeper or lawyer approves operating reconciliation; nothing here touches trust.
edge: client payment deposited to operating that should be trust: raise trust exception, transfer within rule time limit (verify)
processor fee debited from operating vs trust
screens.reg: LSO requires general account receipts and disbursements books and a fees book or chronological bill file (BL9, verify). We do not aim to replace a full GL (deliberately different); we export.

screens.name: Retainer coverage
screens.purpose: Per matter, compare work not yet paid for (unbilled WIP plus receivables) with trust held and the minimum, to see where a top-up is needed.
screens.layout: Filter bar (lawyer, client, shortfall only); table of matters; side panel with the drafted top-up request.

fields.name: unbilled_wip
fields.note: unbilled time and disbursements

fields.name: receivables
fields.note: delivered, unpaid bills

fields.name: protected_amount
fields.note: reserved for a stated purpose; not available for fees

fields.name: minimum_balance
fields.note: from matter trust settings / evergreen

fields.name: shortfall
fields.note: WIP + receivables + minimum - (trust - protected), floored at 0

actions.name: Draft top-up request
actions.note: creates a retainer request draft in billing; lawyer approves and sends

actions.name: Export
actions.note: CSV or PDF

screens.agent: Recomputes nightly; drafts top-up requests for matters with a shortfall, with the numbers that drove it.
screens.gate: Lawyer approves each top-up request before it reaches the client.
edge: protected funds counted as unavailable
flat-fee matter: WIP excluded, only stage fees due
matter with no trust and no minimum: listed only if receivables exist
screens.reg: Money for fees may be taken from trust only after a bill is delivered (BL9 s.10, verify); this report never moves money.

screens.name: Trust interest allocation
screens.purpose: Compute and allocate interest earned on separate interest-bearing trust accounts to the client they belong to.
screens.layout: Account picker and period; rate inputs; per-client allocation table; post button.

fields.name: account
fields.note: separate interest-bearing trust accounts only; mixed trust accounts are excluded

fields.name: rate
fields.note: from the bank statement

fields.name: compounding
fields.note: daily | monthly | none

fields.name: bank_interest_posted
fields.note: amount the bank credited

fields.name: allocation
fields.note: client, matter, computed interest; difference to bank figure shown

actions.name: Post interest to client ledgers
actions.note: lawyer approves; posts trust journal lines

screens.agent: Computes per-client interest from daily balances and flags differences from the bank's credited amount.
screens.gate: Lawyer approves the allocation before interest is posted to client ledgers.
edge: computed total differs from bank credit by more than rounding: blocked until explained
mixed trust account selected: refused, interest belongs to the Law Foundation of Ontario (verify)
screens.reg: Interest on a mixed trust account goes to the Law Foundation of Ontario, not clients; a separate interest-bearing account earns interest for the client (Law Society Act s.57, verify).

agent_jobs.name: bank-feed-sync
agent_jobs.trigger: schedule (daily, plus when a statement is uploaded)
agent_jobs.does: Imports bank lines, de-duplicates them, matches them to journal lines and turns unknown deposits into proposed receipts
agent_jobs.output: proposed receipts for G6; match suggestions

agent_jobs.name: daily-three-way-match
agent_jobs.does: Compares bank, journal and the sum of ledgers for each account, and checks for negative ledgers, cash tallies and dormant balances
agent_jobs.output: exceptions on trust overview, daily digest

agent_jobs.name: withdrawal-drafter
agent_jobs.trigger: event (bill delivered with trust applied; closing; client direction)
agent_jobs.does: Drafts the withdrawal request, runs the permitted-purpose, balance, condition and payee checks, and generates Form 9A

agent_jobs.name: payee-fraud-check
agent_jobs.does: Compares the bank details with known payees and requires a callback record
agent_jobs.output: block or pass on withdrawal checks

agent_jobs.name: month-end-reconciliation
agent_jobs.does: Builds the comparison, the reconciling items, the client listing and the variance explanations, then reminds the lawyer at day 15 and day 22

agent_jobs.name: retainer-replenishment
agent_jobs.does: Drafts a top-up request to the client

agent_jobs.name: dormant-balance-sweep
agent_jobs.does: Lists ledgers with no activity and balances held for two years or more, and drafts client contact steps or an unclaimed-funds application
agent_jobs.output: task list; draft LSO unclaimed-funds request for G11

agent_jobs.name: annual-report-prep
agent_jobs.does: Computes the trust answers for the annual report and links the evidence

agent_jobs.name: audit-chain-verify
agent_jobs.does: Verifies the hash chain and the retention locks

agent_jobs.name: retainer-coverage-scan
agent_jobs.does: Compute WIP + receivables vs available trust and minimum per matter
agent_jobs.output: draft retainer top-up requests for lawyer approval

open_questions: Uncleared funds: hard block on withdrawals against uncleared deposits, or allow a lawyer override with a reason?
Must every withdrawal require dual authorization (two people), or should this be a per-firm setting with single-licensee as the minimum the by-law allows?

Will we integrate directly with banks for EFT initiation (an API) or only produce Form 9A plus a read-only feed, leaving the person to key the transfer in online banking? The second option is lower risk for v1.
Which Canadian banks or aggregators can supply read-only trust account feeds with data held in Canada?
Teranet: do we support Form 9B records for real-estate firms in v1?
Is paralegal (P1) trust accounting in scope? Same by-law, but the annual report questions differ (verify)
Should the app keep the general (operating) account books too, or only the trust books plus a sync to QuickBooks or Xero?
Valuable property held in trust (BL9 s.18(9) record): add a small register screen in v1?
Fiscal year: per licensee or per firm, which affects the retention clock and the annual report.
Do we ship operating books (general journals, vendor bills) or only an export to the firm's accounting system?
Unclaimed trust funds: do we file the LSO application or only draft it?
Could: require written client authorization file on every matter-to-matter transfer (now required) - also for client-to-matter moves?
Could: Alberta and BC law society report packs after Ontario v1?
Is the BL9 retention period for reconciliation packages 10 years before the most recent fiscal year end? (verify against By-Law 9 text)
